title: One dictionary, three contexts
blurb: Passes the same CanvasToneMapping { mode } dictionary into Canvas 2D getContext, WebGL drawingBufferToneMapping(), and WebGPU configure() to compare per-context reflection.
question: Do Canvas 2D, WebGL, and WebGPU accept and reflect the shared CanvasToneMapping { mode } dictionary consistently in the same browser?
result: In Chrome 153 headless with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features and --enable-unsafe-webgpu, WebGPU reports MATCH ({ mode: 'extended' }), Canvas 2D reports MISMATCH (reflects 'standard'), and WebGL reports unsupported because gl.drawingBufferToneMapping is absent. Three-context parity requires Chrome 160+ and WebGLToneMapping.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 158.0.8127.36 (Linux, headless, SDR) with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features on 2026-11-28; earlier Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12

friction.summary: CanvasToneMapping support is split across three separate flags and rollout timelines for WebGPU, Canvas 2D, and WebGL
friction.repro: Pass { mode: 'extended' } to 2D, WebGL, and WebGPU in Chrome 153 with experimental features enabled: WebGPU reflects 'extended', 2D reflects 'standard', and gl.drawingBufferToneMapping is undefined.
friction.workaround: Feature-detect each context type's reflection method separately (getContextAttributes, typeof gl.drawingBufferToneMapping === 'function', and gpuCtx.getConfiguration) rather than assuming unified availability.
